text.p: Lithuania's state-run agricultural bank said on Thursday that its 1996 profit after taxes slipped to 25.5 million litas from 26.43 million litas the previous year.
The bank also said in a statement of audited results that its total income was 160.87 million litas in 1996 versus 112.1 million litas the previous year.
It added that its profit before taxation was 30.75 million litas compared with 30.81 million litas in 1995.
It said that its provision for loan losses was 35.63 million litas versus 1.018 million litas the year before.
The bank's assets grew to 1.27 billion litas in 1996 from 1.145 billion litas at the end of 1995.
Its share capital at the end of the year was 128 million litas, up from 20 million litas the previous year.
In terms of assets, the Agricultural bank is the largest of the country's three state-run banks and second largest in terms of share capital.
The government has said it intends to privatise the bank after it sells off the troubled State Commercial Bank later this year.
A number of private banks in Lithuania, including Hermis Bank and Vilniaus Bank, have expressed an interest in participating in the privatisation of state banks.
